To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

retarded children can be induced to exercise by the use of a simple operant conditioning program and that the children's rate of exercise can be increased to a high level by a progressive schedule of reinforcement.
retarded children will work at a high level for extended periods of time when the work is reinforced by a schedule of social reinforcement.

retarded children will work on a treadmill for a long period of time if the work is contingent on the presentation of an interesting stimulus, and that the rate of work is a function of the schedule of reinforcement.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of whether work responses can (1) be shaped, (2) be maintained for long periods of time, and (3) be maintained by schedules of reinforcement that are simple to administer and do not require elaborate programming of the reinforcement contingencies.
two problems: (1) Can work responses be shaped and sustained by operant procedures in humans? and (2) Can the operant control of work be extended over a long period of time?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is little evidence that work is under the control of operant contingencies, although it is not clear that such evidence could be obtained.
the behavior of human subjects has not yet been subjected to systematic operant conditioning in a manner comparable to that used with lower organisms.
the operant conditioning of work in humans has not been demonstrated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the behavior of retarded children is not readily controllable.
the operant conditioning of work responses in human beings has been demonstrated, but only in the short run and under highly controlled laboratory conditions.

we have shown that a high energy expenditure response (work) can be controlled by a simple schedule of reinforcement (variable interval) and that the response can be sustained over an indefinite period of time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to control work in a human subject.
it is possible to control work behavior of human subjects.
exercise can be a very powerful reinforcer for children with developmental disabilities.
